english_classification.chapter_note: The chapter preserves a three-name cosmological teaching about the First Man ('approved', 'righteous', 'only begotten') in ¶3–5, which is genuine substrate — systematic, impersonal explanation of cosmic epithets with both mapping sides staying within the cosmic system (aeons of light, the enemy, the Father, five sons). Paragraph 8 contains a substrate description of the First Man's cosmic function (standing firm in Darkness, purifying, freeing). The editorial layer then applies these cosmic attributes to the community (¶6, ¶9–10), with ¶4 showing institutional vocabulary ('catechumen') inserted into substrate teaching. Heavy lacunae throughout limit confidence. Gardner's synopsis confirms the Christological/exhortative editorial purpose. Moderate editorial fatigue with exhortation surging in the second half.
